title: Bulk Buying Is a $1,800 Trap That Feels Like Saving
hook: You think buying in bulk saves money — scientists proved it actually makes you spend $1,800 more every year.
angle: Completely counterintuitive: the 'smart saver' behavior of bulk buying is psychologically engineered to make you consume more, waste more, and spend more. Backed by Wharton and University of Chicago research on pantry packing and consumption rates.
audience: Budget-conscious shoppers, Costco/Sam's Club members, families trying to cut grocery bills
key_numbers: $1,800 extra spent per bulk-buying household annually
30% faster consumption when pantry is full (Wharton study)
40% higher food waste in bulk-buying households
$147 average annual warehouse club membership fee
$800+ in in-store impulse buys per bulk-shopping household
